rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mihrab is the prayer place from which Zechariah appeared to his people; it is an elevated, honored place, as shown by David’s mihrab.
rows.anchor: أي أشرف عليهم من المصلى. والمحراب أرفع المواضع، وأشرف المجالس

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: One etymology derives mihrab from warfare: its occupant fights Satan and the passions.
rows.anchor: فقالت فرقة: هو مأخوذ من الحرب كأن ملازمه يحارب الشيطان والشهوات

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another etymology derives mihrab from hardship and toil associated with remaining there.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة: هو مأخوذ من الحرب بفتح الراء كأن ملازمه يلقى منه حربا وتعبا ونصبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse indicates that their prayer leader could stand above the congregation; jurists disagreed about this practice.
rows.anchor: هذه الآية تدل على أن ارتفاع إمامهم على المأمومين كان مشروعا عندهم

rows.speaker: أحمد بن حنبل
rows.claim: Ahmad and others permit an elevated prayer leader, relying on the Prophet’s pulpit prayer.
rows.anchor: فأجاز ذلك الإمام أحمد بن حنبل وغيره متمسكا بقصة المنبر

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik forbids a substantial height but allows a slight one; his associates cite fear of arrogance in the imam.
rows.anchor: ومنع مالك ذلك في الارتفاع الكثير دون اليسير، وعلل أصحابه المنع بخوف الكبر على الإمام

rows.speaker: أبو مسعود
rows.claim: Abu Masud pulled Hudhayfa down when he led from a raised platform; Hudhayfa recalled a prohibition against this.
rows.anchor: أن حذيفة أم الناس بالمدائن على دكان، فأخذ أبو مسعود بقميصه فجبذه

rows.speaker: حذيفة
rows.claim: Hudhayfa reminded the leader that the Companions had been forbidden to lead from a raised position.
rows.anchor: ألم تعلم أنهم كانوا ينهون عن هذا أو ينهى عن ذلك

rows.speaker: عدي بن ثابت الأنصاري
rows.claim: A report from a man who accompanied Ammar says Hudhayfa pulled Ammar down from a platform and cited the Prophet’s prohibition.
rows.anchor: حدثني رجل أنه كان مع عمار بن ياسر بالمدائن

rows.speaker: حذيفة
rows.claim: Hudhayfa quoted the Prophet: when a man leads a congregation, he should not stand higher than their position.
rows.anchor: إذا أم الرجل القوم فلا يقم في مكان أرفع من مقامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi treats the prohibition as established by three Companions and considers the pulpit precedent abrogated because no one invoked it in these disputes.
rows.anchor: فهؤلاء ثلاثة من الصحابة قد أخبروا بالنهي عن ذلك، ولم يحتج أحد منهم على صاحبه بحديث المنبر فدل على أنه منسوخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says the pulpit practice was abrogated because climbing up and down adds actions to prayer, like speech and greeting that were later removed.
rows.anchor: أن فيه عملا زائدا في الصلاة، وهو النزول والصعود، فنسخ كما نسخ الكلام والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi rejects the defense that the Prophet was protected from pride, since many non-arrogant imams could also lead from a height.
rows.anchor: وهذا أولى مما اعتذر به أصحابنا من أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان معصوما من الكبر لأن كثيرا من الأئمة يوجد لا كبر عندهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some excuse the precedent by saying the pulpit’s height was slight.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من علله بأن ارتفاع المنبر كان يسيرا

rows.speaker: الكلبي وقتادة وابن منبه
rows.claim: They interpret Zechariah’s conveying the instruction as a gesture.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي وقتادة وابن منبه: أوحى إليهم أشار

rows.speaker: القتبي
rows.claim: Al-Qutaybi glosses the conveying as signaling.
rows.anchor: أوحى إليهم أشار. القتبي: أومأ

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says Zechariah wrote the instruction on the ground.
rows.anchor: مجاهد: كتب على الأرض. عكرمة

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says Zechariah wrote the instruction in a book.
rows.anchor: كتب على الأرض. عكرمة: كتب في كتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, wahy can mean writing; Qurtubi introduces poetry as evidence for this lexical sense.
rows.anchor: والوحي في كلام العرب الكتابة ومنه قول ذي الرمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhu al-Rumma and Antara use wahy for writing or written marks in their poetry.
rows.anchor:
بقية وحي في بطون الصحائف
وقال عنترة:
كوحي صحائف من عهد كسرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bakratan and ashiyyan are adverbial expressions of time.
rows.anchor: «بكرة وعشيا» ظرفان. وزعم الفراء أن العشي

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says ashiy may be feminine or masculine when indefinite and may also be a plural of ashiyya.
rows.anchor: وزعم الفراء أن العشي يؤنث ويجوز تذكيره إذا أبهمت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi notes that the legal treatment of gestures was discussed earlier under Aal Imran.
rows.anchor: قد تقدم الحكم في الإشارة في «آل عمران

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik first held that writing or sending a messenger breaks an oath not to speak, unless the swearer meant face-to-face speech; he later said writing breaks it unless recalled before delivery.
rows.anchor: فقال مالك: إنه يحنث إلا أن ينوي مشافهته، ثم رجع فقال: لا ينوي في الكتاب ويحنث إلا أن يرتجع الكتاب قبل وصوله

rows.speaker: ابن القاسم
rows.claim: Ibn al-Qasim says reading either party’s letter breaks the oath.
rows.anchor: إذا قرأ كتابه حنث، وكذلك لو قرأ الحالف كتاب المحلوف عليه

rows.speaker: أشهب
rows.claim: Ashhab says the swearer does not break the oath merely by reading the other person’s letter.
rows.anchor: وقال أشهب: لا يحنث إذا قرأه الحالف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi agrees with Ashhab unless the oath meant not to learn the other person’s words; in that case reading breaks it, which explains Ibn al-Qasim’s view.
rows.anchor: وهذا بين لأنه لم يكلمه ولا ابتدأه بكلام، إلا أن يريد ألا يعلم معنى كلامه فإنه يحنث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A vow to speak to someone is fulfilled only by addressing that person face-to-face.
rows.anchor: فإن حلف ليكلمنه لم يبر إلا بمشافهته

rows.speaker: ابن الماجشون
rows.claim: Ibn al-Majishun says a duty to inform someone is fulfilled by writing or sending a messenger, but not if both already know, since their knowledge differs.
rows.anchor: فكتب إليه أو أرسل إليه رسولا بر، ولو علماه جميعا لم يبر، حتى يعلمه

rows.speaker: مالك والشافعي والكوفيون
rows.claim: Malik, al-Shafi‘i, and the Kufans agree that a mute person’s written divorce in his own hand takes effect.
rows.anchor: واتفق مالك والشافعي والكوفيون أن الأخرس إذا كتب الطلاق بيده لزمه

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Kufans make an exception for temporary muteness lasting only days; writing divorce then has no effect.
rows.anchor: إلا أن يكون رجل أصمت أياما فكتب لم يجز من ذلك شيء

rows.speaker: الطحاوي
rows.claim: Al-Tahawi distinguishes lasting muteness from temporary silence, just as hopeless impotence differs from temporary sexual incapacity in a wife’s separation claim.
rows.anchor: الخرس مخالف للصمت العارض، كما أن العجز عن الجماع العارض لمرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account omits the birth narrative: God addresses the newborn Yahya, an ellipsis whose meaning is supplied by context.
rows.anchor: في الكلام حذف المعنى فولد له ولد وقال الله تعالى للمولود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book Yahya is told to grasp is the Torah, without disagreement.
rows.anchor: و«الكتاب» التوراة بلا خلاف. «بقوة» أي

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains grasping the Book with strength as undertaking it earnestly and diligently.
rows.anchor: بقوة» أي بجد واجتهاد قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam explains strength as learning, memorizing, and acting on the Book by obeying commands and avoiding prohibitions.
rows.anchor: العلم به، والحفظ له والعمل به، وهو الالتزام لأوامره، والكف عن نواهيه قاله زيد بن أسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about being given judgment as a child can mean sound judgment and knowledge of its application.
rows.anchor: قيل: الأحكام والمعرفة بها. وروى معمر أن الصبيان

rows.speaker: معمر
rows.claim: Ma‘mar reports that when children invited Yahya to play, he replied that he was not created for play; this is connected to his receiving judgment as a child.
rows.anchor: وروى معمر أن الصبيان قالوا ليحيى: اذهب بنا نلعب فقال: ما للعب خلقت

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Yahya was two or three years old when given judgment.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: كان ابن سنتين أو ثلاث سنين

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says Yahya was three years old.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: كان ابن ثلاث سنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Subiyyan is an accusative circumstantial expression describing Yahya as a child.
rows.anchor: صبيا» نصب على الحال. وقال ابن عباس: من قرأ

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says anyone who recites the Qur’an before puberty is among those given judgment as a child.
rows.anchor: من قرأ القرآن قبل أن يحتلم فهو ممن أوتي الحكم صبيا

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet says every child of Adam comes on Judgment Day with a sin except Yahya ibn Zakariyya; Qurtubi gives no grading here.
rows.anchor: كل بني آدم يأتي يوم القيامة وله ذنب

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Yahya never committed or even contemplated a sin, great or small, and never desired a woman.
rows.anchor: إن يحيى عليه السلام لم يعص الله تعالى قط بصغيرة ولا كبيرة ولا هم بامرأة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says Yahya ate grass and had permanent channels for tears in his cheeks.
rows.anchor: وكان طعام يحيى عليه السلام العشب، وكان للدمع في خديه مجار ثابتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi refers back to his discussion of Yahya as master and chaste in the account of Zakariyya.
rows.anchor:
وقد مضى الكلام في معنى قوله:
وسيدا وحصورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hannan is grammatically coordinated with judgment.
rows.anchor: «حنانا» عطف على «الحكم». وروي عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says he does not know what hannan means.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أنه قال: والله ما أدري ما «الحنان»؟

rows.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
rows.claim: Most commentators understand hannan as compassion, mercy, and love, an act of the inner self.
rows.anchor: الحنان الشفقة والرحمة والمحبة وهو فعل من أفعال النفس

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas transmits two Ibn Abbas explanations: God’s compassionate mercy toward Yahya, or the mercy Yahya was given toward people to rescue them from unbelief and idolatry.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: قال: تعطف الله عز وجل عليه بالرحمة. والقول الآخر ما أعطيه من رحمة الناس حتى يخلصهم من الكفر والشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word derives from a she-camel’s yearning over its young; hananak and hananayk are either synonymous forms or a dual form.
rows.anchor: وأصله من حنين الناقة على ولدها. ويقال: حنانك وحنانيك قيل: هما لغتان

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda says Arabs use hananak or hananayk, O Lord, to mean Your mercy, as in the cited Imru al-Qays poem.
rows.anchor: والعرب تقول: حنانك يا رب وحنانيك يا رب بمعنى واحد تريد رحمتك

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes hannan as mercy, tenderness, and compassion for Yahya’s parents and others.
rows.anchor: رحمة لأبويه وغيرهما وتعطفا وشفقة

rows.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
rows.claim: Ibn al-A‘rabi distinguishes divine Hannan with a doubled n, meaning Merciful, from hannan with a light n, meaning tenderness and mercy; he also records provision and blessing as senses.
rows.anchor: الحنان من صفة الله تعالى مشددا الرحيم. والحنان مخفف: العطف والرحمة

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya records hannan as something sacred or exalted in God, citing Zayd ibn Amr’s vow to make Bilal’s grave a place of devotion; al-Harawi and al-Azhari gloss the story as compassion for him.
rows.anchor: والحنان في كلام العرب أيضا ما عظم من الأمور في ذات الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi concludes that hannan means tenderness, in agreement with Mujahid, whether the tenderness is from God toward Yahya or from Yahya toward creation.
rows.anchor: فالحنان العطف، وكذا قال مجاهد. و«حنانا» أي تعطفا منا عليه أو منه على الخلق

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima interprets hannan as love; the cited poetic usage also describes spouses’ affection.
rows.anchor: عكرمة: محبة. وحنة الرجل امرأته لتوادهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakat here means purification, blessing, and growth in good works, making Yahya a blessing who guides people.
rows.anchor: الزكاة» التطهير والبركة والتنمية في وجوه الخير والبر

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba offers the alternative that Yahya was a charitable gift to his parents.
rows.anchor: زكاة» صدقة به على أبويه قاله ابن قتيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yahya was obedient to God and therefore neither committed a sin nor inclined toward one.
rows.anchor: أي مطيعا لله تعالى، ولهذا لم يعمل خطيئة ولم يلم بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Barr describes Yahya as exceptionally dutiful to his parents; jabbar means arrogant, and the description emphasizes gentleness and humility.
rows.anchor: متكبرا. وهذا وصف ليحيى عليه السلام بلين الجانب وخفض الجناح

rows.speaker: الطبري وغيره
rows.claim: Al-Tabari and others interpret peace upon Yahya as safety.
rows.anchor: قال الطبري وغيره: معناه أمان

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya prefers a greeting from God over mere safety, since safety is a lesser baseline and God’s greeting honors Yahya at life’s vulnerable transitions; Qurtubi calls this a good view.
rows.anchor: والأظهر عندي أنها التحية المتعارفة فهي أشرف وأنبه من الأمان

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Tabari transmits Hasan’s report that Jesus and Yahya, maternal cousins, debated which was better; Jesus said Yahya was honored by God’s greeting, whereas Jesus had greeted himself.
rows.anchor: وذكر الطبري عن الحسن أن عيسى ويحيى التقيا وهما ابنا الخالة

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: Some scholars infer Jesus’s greater rank because he confidently pronounced peace upon himself, while Yahya was greeted by God; Ibn Atiyya says each view has its case.
rows.anchor: فانتزع بعض العلماء من هذه الآية في التسليم فضل عيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This begins a separate story, which Muhammad is told to recount so people recognize God’s complete power.
rows.anchor: هذا ابتداء قصة ليست من الأولى. والخطاب لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم أي عرفهم قصتها ليعرفوا كمال قدرتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Id is an appositional substitute for Mary, since the time contains the events within it; intibadh means withdrawing and separating.
rows.anchor: بدل من «مريم» بدل اشتمال لأن الأحيان مشتملة على ما فيها. والانتباذ الاعتزال والانفراد

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says Mary withdrew to become pure from menstruation or postpartum bleeding.
rows.anchor: فقال السدي: انتبذت لتطهر من حيض أو نفاس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi prefers the view that she withdrew for worship: as a temple servant she sought privacy in its eastern prayer niche.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره: لتعبد الله وهذا حسن

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari reports that eastern directions were honored because sunrise and light come from the east.
rows.anchor: يعظمون جهة المشرق ومن حيث تطلع الأنوار

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the Christians’ east-facing prayer by saying they made Jesus’s birthplace their qibla, reasoning that Mary would have placed him in the best direction.
rows.anchor: إني لأعلم الناس لم اتخذ النصارى المشرق قبلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say Mary was a prophet because an angel was sent to her and spoke with her; others deny this, comparing her vision to the Prophet’s seeing Gabriel as Dihya, but Qurtubi says the first view is stronger.
rows.anchor: واختلف الناس في نبوة مريم فقيل كانت نبية بهذا الإرسال والمحاورة للملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take Our Spirit as Jesus’s spirit, created before bodies and placed in the body God formed in Mary’s womb.
rows.anchor: قيل: هو روح عيسى عليه السلام لأن الله تعالى خلق الأرواح قبل الأجساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others identify the Spirit as Gabriel; the divine possessive marks honor, and the following description makes Gabriel the apparent referent.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو جبريل وأضيف الروح إلى الله تعالى تخصيصا وكرامة. والظاهر أنه جبريل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angel appeared in human form with sound proportions because Mary could not bear to see Gabriel in his actual form.
rows.anchor: سويا } أي مستوي الخلقة لأنها لم تكن لتطيق أو تنظر جبريل في صورته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing an attractive man breach her privacy, Mary feared evil and sought refuge in the Merciful if he was God-fearing.
rows.anchor: إني أعوذ بالرحمن منك إن كنت تقيا

rows.speaker: البكالي
rows.claim: Al-Bakkali says Gabriel recoiled in fear when Mary invoked the Merciful.
rows.anchor: البكالي: فنكص جبريل عليه السلام فزعا من ذكر الرحمن

rows.speaker: الثعلبي
rows.claim: Al-Tha‘labi says she was addressing a righteous man, expressing astonishment through her conditional appeal.
rows.anchor: الثعلبي: كان رجلا صالحا فتعوذت به تعجبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another grammatical interpretation makes taqiyyan passive in sense: someone from whom others must protect themselves.
rows.anchor: وقيل: تقي فعيل بمعنى مفعول أي كنت ممن يتقى منه

rows.speaker: أبو وائل
rows.claim: Abu Wa’il says Mary knew a God-fearing person has self-restraint when she said this.
rows.anchor: البخاري قال أبو وائل: علمت مريم أن التقي ذو نهية

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih says Taqi was the name of a notorious wicked man of that time; Ibn Atiyya calls this conjectural and weak.
rows.anchor: تقي اسم فاجر معروف في ذلك الوقت قاله وهب بن منبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel phrases the gift as his own because he is the one announcing it to Mary.
rows.anchor: جعل الهبة من قبله لما كان الإعلام بها من قبله

rows.speaker: ورش عن نافع
rows.claim: Warsh from Nafi reads liyahaba, making God the giver who sent Gabriel.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ورش عن نافع «ليهب لك» على معنى أرسلني الله ليهب لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation reads the hamzated form according to its intended sense: Gabriel was sent in order to give her a boy.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معنى «لأهب» بالهمز محمول على المعنى أي قال: أرسلته لأهب لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary’s statement that no human had touched her means she had not married; denying prostitution reinforces that this covers both lawful and unlawful intercourse.
rows.anchor: أي بنكاح. { ولم أك بغيا } أي زانية. وذكرت هذا تأكيدا لأن قولها لم يمسسني بشر يشمل الحلال والحرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative says Mary did not doubt God’s power but asked whether the child would come through a future husband or direct creation.
rows.anchor: ما استبعدت من قدرة الله تعالى شيئا ولكن أرادت كيف يكون هذا الولد

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says Gabriel blew into the opening of Mary’s garment and sleeve.
rows.anchor: روي أن جبريل عليه السلام حين قال لها هذه المقالة نفخ في جيب درعها وكمها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Gabriel blew through a finger at the sleeve cuff, and Mary conceived Jesus immediately.
rows.anchor: أخذ جبريل عليه السلام ردن قميصها بإصبعه فنفخ فيه فحملت من ساعتها بعيسى

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari reports Christian claims that Mary was thirteen at conception, Jesus lived thirty-two years and days before being raised, and Mary lived six more years, totaling over fifty.
rows.anchor: وزعمت النصارى أن مريم حملت بعيسى ولها ثلاث عشرة سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose clause has an omitted verb: God creates Jesus to make him a wondrous sign of divine power and a mercy to believers; the decree was written in the Preserved Tablet.
rows.anchor: متعلق بمحذوف أي ونخلقه لنجعله: { آية } دلالة على قدرتنا عجيبة { ورحمة } أي لمن آمن به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary withdrew with the pregnancy to a distant place to avoid her people’s accusation that she had delivered without a husband.
rows.anchor: فرارا من تعيير قومها إياها بالولادة من غير زوج

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas locates the distant place at the far end of the Wadi of Bethlehem, four miles from Jerusalem.
rows.anchor: إلى أقصى الوادي، وهو وادي بيت لحم بينه وبين إيلياء أربعة أميال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says conception was followed immediately by birth; Qurtubi calls this the more apparent reading because withdrawal follows conception in the account.
rows.anchor: ما هو إلا أن حملت فوضعت في الحال وهذا هو الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ajaa means that labor compelled Mary; it is the hamzated causative of ja’a, like bringing someone to a place.
rows.anchor: أجاءها» بمعنى اضطرها وهو تعدية جاء بالهمز

rows.speaker: شيبيل وعاصم
rows.claim: Shubayl, with a transmission from Asim, reads faaja’aha, meaning labor surprised her.
rows.anchor: وقرأ شبيل ورويت عن عاصم «فاجأها» من المفاجأة

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy’s codex has the wording When labor compelled her.
rows.anchor: وفي مصحف أبي «فلما أجاءها المخاض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zuhayr’s line uses aja’ahu for being driven or compelled by fear and hope.
rows.anchor:
وجار سار معتمدا إلينا
أجاءته المخافة والرجاء

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most reciters pronounce al-makhad with an open mim; Ibn Kathir is reported to use a kasra. It means labor, its intensity, and its pains.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «المخاض» بفتح الميم. وابن كثير فيما روي عنه بكسرها وهو الطلق وشدة الولادة وأوجاعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary sought the palm trunk to lean and cling to it during the severe pains of labor; it was a dry, branchless desert trunk.
rows.anchor: كأنها طلبت شيئا تستند إليه وتتعلق به، كما تتعلق الحامل لشدة وجع الطلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary wished for death from religious concern: fear that suspicion and taunting would tempt her, and fear that people would be led into slander; on this basis wishing for death is permissible.
rows.anchor: تمنت مريم عليها السلام الموت من جهة الدين لوجهين: أحدهما: أنها خافت أن يظن بها الشر في دينها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi says he heard that Mary was distressed after a voice called for the one worshiped besides God to come out.
rows.anchor: وقد سمعت أن مريم عليها السلام سمعت نداء من يقول: اخرج يا من يعبد من دون الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasy is an insignificant thing people forget without grieving its loss, such as a tent peg or traveler’s rope; the cited al-Kumayt line uses it for a person of no consequence.
rows.anchor: النسي في كلام العرب الشيء الحقير الذي شأنه أن ينسى ولا يتألم لفقده

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra interprets nasy as the menstrual cloth cast away by a woman, so Mary would mean a discarded menstrual cloth.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: النسي ما تلقيه المرأة من خرق اعتلالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word is read nasy with either vowel on nun as dialect variants, and also with hamza as nasy’an by Muhammad ibn Ka‘b and Nauf al-Bakkali, or with doubled s and no hamza by Bakr ibn Habib.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «نسيا» بفتح النون وهما لغتان مثل الحجر والحجر

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari recounts that Mary and Yahya’s mother were pregnant together; Mary sensed her fetus bowing toward the fetus in her sister’s womb, identified as Yahya.
rows.anchor: أنها لما حملت بعيسى عليه السلام حملت أيضا أختها بيحيى

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi recounts that Mary fled with Joseph the carpenter after he learned she was accused of illicit pregnancy; Gabriel told him Jesus was from the Holy Spirit. Ibn Atiyya calls the story weak.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: قيل ليوسف وكانت سميت له أنها حملت من الزنى

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya judges the story of Mary’s flight with Joseph the carpenter weak.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وهذا كله ضعيف

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says Mary carried Jesus for eight months, prompting the claim that an eight-month infant cannot survive as a special sign of Jesus.
rows.anchor: وتظاهرت الروايات بأنها ولدته لثمانية أشهر. قاله عكرمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other reports say Mary delivered after nine months or six months; Qurtubi says Ibn Abbas’s account of immediate birth is sounder and more apparent.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ولدته لتسعة. وقيل: لستة. وما ذكرناه عن ابن عباس أصح وأظهر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the voice from beneath Mary was Gabriel, and Jesus did not speak until she brought him to her people.
rows.anchor: جبريل، ولم يتكلم عيسى حتى أتت به قومها

rows.speaker: علقمة والضحاك وقتادة
rows.claim: Alqama, al-Dahhak, and Qatada likewise identify the caller as Gabriel rather than the infant Jesus.
rows.anchor: علقمة والضحاك وقتادة ففي هذا لها آية وأمارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angel’s call was a sign to Mary that a supernatural event had a great divine purpose.
rows.anchor: ففي هذا لها آية وأمارة أن هذا من الأمور الخارقة للعادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase not to grieve explains the preceding call and means Mary should not grieve over giving birth.
rows.anchor: وأن» مفسرة بمعنى أي المعنى: فلا تحزني بولادتك

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says the sariyya is Jesus, a noble and excellent man.
rows.anchor: يعني عيسى. والسري من الرجال العظيم الخصال السيد

rows.speaker: جمهور
rows.claim: Most commentators take the sariyya to be a stream near the palm; Ibn Abbas says God restored water to a river that had dried up.
rows.anchor: وقال الجمهور: أشار لها إلى الجدول الذي كان قريب جذع النخلة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says God caused water to flow again in a river that had dried up for Mary.
rows.anchor: كان ذلك نهرا قد انقطع ماؤه فأجراه الله تعالى لمريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sariyya can name a stream because water runs through it, as illustrated by cited poetry.
rows.anchor: والنهر يسمى سريا كأن الماء يسري فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says Jesus called to Mary; this would be a miracle that reassured her, but Qurtubi prefers the stream interpretation.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ناداها عيسى، وكان ذلك معجزة وآية وتسكينا لقلبها والأول أظهر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas recited the phrase as an angel from beneath her; the explanation places Gabriel on lower ground.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس «فناداها ملك من تحتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commands Mary to shake the dry trunk so she can witness another sign: lifeless wood revived.
rows.anchor: أمرها بهز الجذع اليابس لترى آية أخرى في إحياء موات الجذع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition ba in shaking the trunk intensifies the verb; alternatively the meaning is to shake dates down onto her.
rows.anchor: والباء في قوله: «بجذع» زائدة مؤكدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading tusāqiṭ assimilates a ta; Hamza reads lightly without it, Hafs from Asim reads with damma on ta and kasra on qaf, and other readings include several forms with different subjects.
rows.anchor: أي تتساقط فأدغم التاء في السين. وقرأ حمزة «تساقط» مخففا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi lists nine readings of the falling verb; accordingly dates may grammatically fall through the trunk’s action, the shaking, or the palm’s action.
rows.anchor: فهذه تسع قراءات ذكرها الزمخشري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jani means ripe and ready to pick, from the verb for harvesting fruit.
rows.anchor: وجنيا» معناه قد طابت وصلحت للاجتناء، وهي من جنيت الثمرة

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: A reading attributed to Ibn Masud adds barniyyan after ripe dates, but Qurtubi says the report is not sound.
rows.anchor: ويروى عن ابن مسعود ولا يصح أنه قرأ «تساقط عليك رطبا جنيا برنيا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the dates were ajwa.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: «رطبا جنيا» قال: كانت عجوة

rows.speaker: عباس بن الفضل
rows.claim: Abbas ibn al-Fadl reports Abu Amr’s explanation that jani means fresh, neither dried nor far from the picker’s hand; Qurtubi calls this correct.
rows.anchor: سألت أبا عمرو بن العلاء عن قوله: «رطبا جنيا» فقال: لم يذو

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra treats jani and majni as equivalent passive forms, like slain and wounded.
rows.anchor: الجني والمجني واحد يذهب إلى أنهما بمنزلة القتيل والمقتول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other philologists define jani as fruit cut from one tree and taken from where it grew, citing a poem about nearby fruit harvest.
rows.anchor: الجني المقطوع من نخلة واحدة، والمأخوذ من مكان نشأته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the dry palm rapidly grew fronds and fruit, ripened through each stage in an instant, then dropped dates into Mary’s hands without bruising them.
rows.anchor: كان جذعا نخزا فلما هزت نظرت إلى أعلى الجذع فإذا السعف قد طلع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some infer that although provision is decreed, God assigns people effort: Mary was ordered to shake the tree even though the sign could have occurred without shaking.
rows.anchor: استدل بعض الناس من هذه الآية على أن الرزق وإن كان محتوما فإن الله تعالى قد وكل ابن آدم إلى سعي ما فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earning one’s provision is God’s customary order and does not undermine trust, contrary to ignorant ascetics; Mary had earlier received provision without work.
rows.anchor: الأمر بتكليف الكسب في الرزق سنة الله تعالى في عباده، وأن ذلك لا يقدح في التوكل

rows.speaker: علماؤنا
rows.claim: The scholars explain that before birth Mary’s heart was unoccupied and her body spared exertion; after she became absorbed in her child, God returned her to ordinary reliance on means.
rows.anchor: لما كان قلبها فارغا فرغ الله جارحتها عن النصب، فلما ولدت عيسى وتعلق قلبها بحبه

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says Mary answered Jesus that she had no husband or master and feared people’s judgment, so Jesus promised to speak for her.
rows.anchor: لا ذات زوج ولا مملوكة! أي شيء عذري عند الناس

rows.speaker: الربيع بن خثيم
rows.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Khuthaym recommends dates as the best food for a postpartum woman, reasoning that God would have fed Mary something better if it existed.
rows.anchor: ما للنفساء عندي خير من الرطب لهذه الآية، ولو علم الله شيئا هو أفضل من الرطب للنفساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dates became customary for postpartum women from Mary’s story, as did tahnik; another view recommends dates for difficult birth and honey for illness.
rows.anchor: ولذلك قالوا: التمر عادة للنفساء من ذلك الوقت، وكذلك التحنيك

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says dates are best when labor is difficult and honey best for the sick.
rows.anchor: ولا للمريض خير من العسل ذكره الزمخشري

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik says jani dates are naturally ripe without naqsh; artificially accelerating ripening is disfavored and does not make them legally ripe or saleable as ripe fruit.
rows.anchor: الجني من التمر ما طاب من غير نقش ولا إفساد

rows.speaker: طلحة بن سليمان
rows.claim: Talha ibn Sulayman reads jani with a kasra on jim for vowel harmony.
rows.anchor: وعن طلحة بن سليمان «جنيا» بكسر الجيم للإتباع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary is told to eat dates, drink from the stream, and find comfort in seeing her prophetic child; the two provisions also soothe her because they are miracles.
rows.anchor: أي فكلي من الجني، واشربي من السري، وقري عينا برؤية الولد النبي

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most reciters read qirri with an open qaf; al-Tabari also transmits a kasra reading used in Najd.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بفتح القاف وهي قراءة الجمهور. وحكى الطبري قراءة «وقري» بكسر القاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aynan is an accusative of specification: the eye is really the actor, transferred grammatically to its owner; Qurtubi gives several parallel expressions.
rows.anchor: «عينا» نصب على التمييز كقولك: طب نفسا. والفعل

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Amr explains God’s making an eye cool as putting it to sleep and ending wakefulness.
rows.anchor: أقر الله عينه أي أنام عينه، وأذهب سهره

rows.speaker: الشيباني
rows.claim: Al-Shaybani takes the phrase to mean sleeping, urging Mary to eat, drink, and rest.
rows.anchor: وقال الشيباني: «وقري عينا» معناه نامي حضها على الأكل والشرب والنوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase cool the eye is explained through the contrast of cool joyful tears and hot grief tears; another group rejects this because all tears are warm and explains it as a calm, settled gaze.
rows.anchor: ودمعة السرور باردة، ودمعة الحزن حارة. وضعفت فرقة هذا وقالت: الدمع كله حار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tarayinna develops from tar’ayayna through elision and vowel transfer; after the jussive nun drops, the emphatic nun is added and the feminine ya is kasra-marked at the meeting of two sukuns.
rows.anchor: الأصل في ترين ترأيين فحذفت الهمزة كما حذفت من ترى ونقلت فتحتها إلى الراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic nun is licensed here by the connective ma, just as a lām of oath can prepare for it; Ibn Durayd and al-Afwah provide parallel poetic forms.
rows.anchor: وإنما دخلت النون هنا بتوطئة «ما» كما يوطىء لدخولها أيضا لام القسم

rows.speaker: طلحة وأبو جعفر وشيبة
rows.claim: Talha, Abu Ja‘far, and Shayba read tarin with a still ya and a light, open nun; Abu al-Fath calls the reading anomalous.
rows.anchor: وقرأ طلحة وأبو جعفر وشيبة «ترين» بسكون الياء وفتح النون خفيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to say she vowed a fast is the conditional answer, with an omitted clause for anyone asking about the child.
rows.anchor:
هذا 
جواب الشرط وفيه إضمار أي فسألك عن ولدك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وأنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Anas explain sawm as silence, since both fasting and silence are forms of abstention.
rows.anchor: أي صمتا قاله ابن عباس وأنس بن مالك

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy ibn Ka‘b’s reading adds samtan as an explanatory gloss; Anas also transmits a version with a conjunction before silence.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة أبي بن كعب «إني نذرت للرحمن صوما صمتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extra words and differing conjunction show that silence is explanatory rather than Qur’anic wording; if joined by wa, silence could be a separate practice.
rows.anchor: واختلاف اللفظين يدل على أن الحرف ذكر تفسيرا لا قرآنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports from hadith scholars and linguists consistently use sawm for silence because both terms mean withholding.
rows.anchor: والذي تتابعت به الأخبار عن أهل الحديث ورواة اللغة أن الصوم هو الصمت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative takes sawm as ordinary fasting, during which their custom required silence except for gestures; this also explains Anas’s reading with wa.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو الصوم المعروف، وكان يلزمهم الصمت يوم الصوم إلا بالإشارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the alternative, silence was bound by vow to fasting, like a vow to walk to the House requiring pilgrimage or umra.
rows.anchor: وأن الصمت كان عندهم في الصوم ملتزما بالنذر، كما أن من نذر منا المشي إلى البيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God instructed Mary, through Gabriel or her son according to the earlier disagreement, not to speak to people and to direct their questions to the child, lifting her embarrassment and proving her innocence.
rows.anchor: أن الله تعالى أمرها على لسان جبريل عليه السلام أو ابنها على الخلاف المتقدم بأن تمسك عن مخاطبة البشر

rows.speaker: جمهور
rows.claim: The apparent wording permits Mary to speak the prescribed sentence; this is the majority view.
rows.anchor: وظاهر الآية أنها أبيح لها أن تقول هذه الألفاظ التي في الآية، وهو قول الجمهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After seeing the signs and trusting that God would clear her, Mary returned carrying Jesus from her place of withdrawal.
rows.anchor: روي أن مريم لما اطمأنت بما رأت من الآيات، وعلمت أن الله تعالى سيبين عذرها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Mary left at sunrise and arrived around noon with the child, with pregnancy and birth occurring within three daylight hours.
rows.anchor: خرجت من عندهم حين أشرقت الشمس، فجاءتهم عند الظهر ومعها صبي تحمله

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says Mary gave birth unnoticed, remained in postpartum seclusion for forty days, and then returned carrying the child.
rows.anchor: ولدت حيث لم يشعر بها قومها، ومكثت أربعين يوما للنفاس

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid interprets fariyyan as something immense.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: «فريا» عظيما. وقال سعيد بن مسعدة

rows.speaker: سعيد بن مسعدة
rows.claim: Sa‘id ibn Mus‘ada glosses fariyyan as an invented, fabricated matter and says fara and afra mean the same.
rows.anchor: أي مختلقا مفتعلا يقال: فريت وأفريت بمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The charge implies an invented child attributed to a husband who is not its father, like the Qur’anic description of women’s false claims.
rows.anchor: والولد من الزنى كالشيء المفترى

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة والأخفش
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda and al-Akhfash gloss fariyyan as an astonishing, unprecedented marvel.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: الفري العجيب النادر وقاله الأخفش

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Qutrub says fariyyan means newly made leather water-skins, hence a new and unprecedented matter.
rows.anchor: وقال قطرب: الفري الجديد من الأسقية أي جئت بأمر جديد بديع

rows.speaker: أبو حيوة
rows.claim: Abu Haywa reads fariyyan with a still ra.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة: «شيئا فريا» بسكون الراء

rows.speaker: السدي ووهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Al-Suddi and Wahb ibn Munabbih report that when a woman reached to strike Mary, God paralyzed half her body.
rows.anchor: السدي ووهب بن منبه: لما أتت به قومها تحمله تسامع بذلك بنو إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says God made a suspected accuser mute, so people refrained from striking Mary or insulting her and spoke gently.
rows.anchor: فأخرسه الله تعالى فتحامى الناس من أن يضربوها، أو يقولوا لها كلمة تؤذيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some identify Harun as Moses’s brother and say the reproach compares Mary to a person thought as devout as Harun; kinship language may refer to descent from him.
rows.anchor: هو هارون أخو موسى والمراد من كنا نظنها مثل هارون في العبادة

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says Harun was Mary’s paternal brother, a common name used in reverence for Moses’s brother, and an exemplary Israelite.
rows.anchor: كان لها أخ من أبيها اسمه هارون لأن هذا الاسم كان كثيرا في بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says Harun was a righteous contemporary whose funeral was followed by forty thousand men named Harun.
rows.anchor: هارون هذا رجل صالح في ذلك الزمان تبع جنازته يوم مات أربعون ألفا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says a devout Israelite named Harun served at the sanctuary, and Mary was associated with his way of worship.
rows.anchor: كان في ذلك الزمان في بني إسرائيل عابد منقطع إلى الله عز وجل يسمى هارون

rows.speaker: كعب الأحبار
rows.claim: Ka‘b al-Ahbar told Aisha that Mary was not Moses’s sister; he said the two figures were separated by six hundred years unless the Prophet had stated otherwise, at which Aisha fell silent.
rows.anchor: إن مريم ليست بأخت هارون أخي موسى

rows.speaker: المغيرة بن شعبة
rows.claim: In Sahih Muslim, al-Mughira says Christians at Najran asked him about Mary being called Aaron’s sister despite the centuries between Moses and Jesus; the Prophet answered that people named after earlier prophets and righteous figures.
rows.anchor:
صحيح مسلم
" عن المغيرة بن شعبة قال: لما قدمت نجران سألوني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi concludes the name simply matched an earlier name and infers that naming children after prophets is permitted.
rows.anchor: والمعنى أنه اسم وافق اسما. ويستفاد من هذا جواز التسمية بأسماء الأنبياء

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says a millennium or more separated Mary from Moses and Aaron, so she was not their literal sister; if related, the expression means descendant or fellow member of their people.
rows.anchor: كان بينهما وبينه ألف سنة أو أكثر فلا يتخيل أن مريم كانت أخت موسى وهارون

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya transmits an alternative that Harun was a wicked contemporary whose name was used to shame Mary; Qurtubi traces the claim to Sa‘id ibn Jubayr and says the implication is that her parents were not suited to such conduct.
rows.anchor: بل كان في ذلك الزمان رجل فاجر اسمه هارون فنسبوها إليه على جهة التعيير والتوبيخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi says that, on the wicked-Harun interpretation, their indirect accusation legally entails the hadd for slander.
rows.anchor: وهذا من التعريض الذي يقوم مقام التصريح. وذلك يوجب عندنا الحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi rejects the wicked-Harun interpretation because the authentic hadith explicitly explains the naming custom and leaves no room for dispute.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول الأخير يرده الحديث الصحيح، وهو نص صريح فلا كلام لأحد معه

rows.speaker: عمر بن لجأ التيمي
rows.claim: Umar ibn Laja al-Taymi reads the phrase with abak rather than abuki.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عمر بن لجأ التيمي «ما كان أباك امرأ سوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary kept the instruction not to speak; the verse says she gestured rather than uttering the vow formula, supporting an interpretation of say as signal.
rows.anchor: التزمت مريم عليها السلام ما أمرت به من ترك الكلام، ولم يرد في هذه الآية أنها نطقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people thought Mary’s gesture showed contempt worse than her alleged adultery and asked how they could speak to an infant.
rows.anchor: استخفافها بنا أشد علينا من زناها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kana here refers to the child’s present state, not the past, since everyone once was an infant.
rows.anchor: هنا ليس يراد بها الماضي لأن كل واحد قد كان في المهد صبيا، وإنما هي في معنى هو الآن

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda treats kana as redundant, citing a poetic example.
rows.anchor:
وقال أبو عبيدة: «كان» هنا لغو كما قال:
وجيران لنا كانوا كرام

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari rejects taking kana as redundant because it governs the predicate, and rejects the meaning came to be because that reading would not need a predicate.
rows.anchor: لا يجوز أن يقال زائدة وقد نصبت «صبيا»، ولا أن يقال «كان» بمعنى حدث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi prefers reading man as conditional and kana as yakun: how can they speak to one who is an infant in the cradle? A past verb can express present or future in a conditional.
rows.anchor: بمعنى يكن والتقدير: من يكن في المهد صبيا فكيف نكلمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cradle may be a raised bed, the mother’s lap, or a way to say that a small child should be sleeping there.
rows.anchor: والمهد» قيل: كان سريرا كالمهد. وقيل: «المهد» هاهنا حجر الأم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says Jesus had been nursing, stopped when he heard the people, turned toward them, leaned on his left, and pointed with his right index finger before speaking.
rows.anchor: فقيل: كان عيسى عليه السلام يرضع فلما سمع كلامهم ترك الرضاعة وأقبل عليهم بوجهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus first declares himself God’s servant, affirming God’s lordship and answering those who later exaggerated his status.
rows.anchor: فكان أول ما نطق به الاعتراف بعبوديته لله تعالى وربوبيته، ردا على من غلا من بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The view that Jesus received the Gospel as a delivered book in the cradle and immediately understood, taught, fasted, and prayed is extremely weak.
rows.anchor: قيل: آتاه في تلك الحالة الكتاب، وفهمه وعلمه، وآتاه النبوة كما علم آدم الأسماء كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi prefers that the Book and prophethood had been decreed for Jesus eternally, although no scripture was revealed to him at that moment.
rows.anchor: أي حكم لي بإيتاء الكتاب والنبوة في الأزل، وإن لم يكن الكتاب منزلا في الحال وهذا أصح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus is made a source of religious blessing and benefit, teaching people and calling them to the faith.
rows.anchor: أي ذا بركات ومنافع في الدين والدعاء إليه ومعلما له

rows.speaker: التستري
rows.claim: Al-Tustari explains Jesus’s blessing as enjoining right, forbidding wrong, guiding the lost, defending the oppressed, and helping the distressed.
rows.anchor: وجعلني آمر بالمعروف، وأنهى عن المنكر، وأرشد الضال، وأنصر المظلوم، وأغيث الملهوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus was enjoined to perform prayer and zakat once accountable and able; Qurtubi adopts this reading and takes ma dumtu hayyan as the duration of his life.
rows.anchor: أي لأؤديهما إذا أدركني التكليف، وأمكنني أداؤهما، على القول الأخير الصحيح

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Jesus’s naming his mother, rather than a father, shows that this was divinely inspired speech.
rows.anchor: لما قال «وبرا بوالدتي» ولم يقل بوالدي علم أنه شيء من جهة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jabbar means a proud tyrant who kills and strikes in anger; another definition is someone who recognizes no one’s right over him.
rows.anchor: أي متعظما متكبرا يقتل ويضرب على الغضب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses shaqiyyan as disobedient to his mother.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس: عاقا. وقيل: عاصيا لربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations take shaqiyyan as a failure of goodness, disobedience to God, or abandonment of God’s command like Satan.
rows.anchor: وقيل: عاصيا لربه. وقيل: لم يجعلني تاركا لأمره

rows.speaker: مالك بن أنس
rows.claim: Malik says the statement is difficult for advocates of human free creation: Jesus reports God’s decree of his future through death.
rows.anchor: ما أشدها على أهل القدر! أخبر عيسى عليه السلام بما قضى من أمره

rows.speaker: ابن زيد وغيره
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd and others report that the listeners submitted when they heard Jesus speak, acknowledging the matter was extraordinary.
rows.anchor: أنهم لما سمعوا كلام عيسى أذعنوا وقالوا: إن هذا لأمر عظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi says Jesus spoke miraculously once to clear his mother, then resumed ordinary childhood; there is no report of continuous speech or worship, which would not have gone unnoticed, so the claim that he remained articulate from birth is false.
rows.anchor: ثم عاد إلى حالة الأطفال، حتى مشى على عادة البشر إلى أن بلغ مبلغ الصبيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus’s infant speech also refutes Jews and Christians who deny that he spoke in the cradle; consensus that Mary was not punished supports the miracle’s proof of innocence.
rows.anchor: ويدل أيضا على أنه تكلم في المهد خلافا لليهود والنصارى. والدليل على ذلك إجماع الفرق على أنها لم تحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer, zakat, and honoring parents were binding on earlier communities and remained established in Muhammad’s law.
rows.anchor: ودلت هذه الآية على أن الصلاة والزكاة وبر الوالدين كان واجبا على الأمم السالفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus lived with great humility: he ate wild plants, wore rough hair cloth, sat on earth, and had no home, staying wherever night found him.
rows.anchor: وكان عيسى عليه السلام في غاية التواضع يأكل الشجر، ويلبس الشعر، ويجلس على التراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A gesture can function as speech and convey its meaning; Mary’s gesture was understood by her people.
rows.anchor: الإشارة بمنزلة الكلام، وتفهم ما يفهم القول

rows.speaker: الكوفيون والشعبي والأوزاعي وأحمد وإسحاق
rows.claim: The Kufans, al-Sha‘bi, al-Awza‘i, Ahmad, and Ishaq say a mute person cannot commit slander by accusation or perform li‘an, because slander requires explicit wording and li‘an is testimony.
rows.anchor: لا يصح قذف الأخرس ولا لعانه

rows.speaker: ابن القصار
rows.claim: Ibn al-Qassar rejects their argument: if non-Arab speech can state slander, a mute person’s gesture should likewise suffice.
rows.anchor: قولهم إن القذف لا يصح إلا بالتصريح فهو باطل بسائر الألسنة ما عدا العربية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi says the claim of consensus against a mute person’s testimony is mistaken; Malik accepts intelligible signs as testimony, though someone able to speak must use words.
rows.anchor: وما ذكروه من الإجماع في شهادة الأخرس فغلط. وقد نص مالك أن شهادته مقبولة إذا فهمت إشارته

rows.speaker: ابن المنذر
rows.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir argues that those who enforce a mute person’s divorce, sales, and other acts should also enforce slander by gesture.
rows.anchor: يلزمون الأخرس الطلاق والبيوع وسائر الأحكام، فينبغي أن يكون القذف مثل ذلك

rows.speaker: المهلب
rows.claim: Al-Muhallab says gesture can be stronger than speech, as the Prophet indicated the nearness of the Hour by comparing two fingers; direct perception can outweigh reports.
rows.anchor: وقد تكون الإشارة في كثير من أبواب الفقه أقوى من الكلام

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains that the second occurrence of al-salam has the definite article because the earlier one lacked it.
rows.anchor: ذكر السلام قبل هذا بغير ألف ولام فحسن في الثانية ذكر الألف واللام

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi explains the three greetings as peace for Jesus in worldly life, the grave, and resurrection, his three states of being alive, dead, and raised.
rows.anchor: لأن له أحوالا ثلاثة: في الدنيا حيا، وفي القبر ميتا، وفي الآخرة مبعوثا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The birth greeting can alternatively mean protection from Satan’s whispering, as discussed under Aal Imran; Jesus then stopped speaking in the cradle until boyhood.
rows.anchor: وقيل: من همز الشيطان كما تقدم في «آل عمران

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada recounts a woman telling Jesus that his womb and nursing mother were blessed; Jesus replied that those who read, follow, and practice God’s Book are blessed.
rows.anchor: طوبى للبطن الذي حملك، والثدي الذي أرضعك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus is to be understood as Mary’s son, not the illegitimate child or son of Joseph claimed by Jews, nor God or God’s son as Christians claim.
rows.anchor: لا كما تقول اليهود إنه لغير رشدة، وأنه ابن يوسف النجار، ولا كما قالت النصارى: إنه الإله أو ابن الإله

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisa’i parses qawla al-haqq as an adjective of Jesus and relates the title to the Word of God and to God as the Truth.
rows.anchor: قول الحق» نعت لعيسى أي ذلك عيسى ابن مريم قول الحق

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: Abu Hatim takes the phrase to mean that this is the true statement.
rows.anchor: حاتم: المعنى هو قول الحق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says it means Jesus’s speech is true, not false; the genitive construction resembles a true promise and the abode of the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: يريد هذا كلام عيسى بن مريم صلى الله عليه وسلم قول الحق ليس بباطل

rows.speaker: عاصم وعبد الله بن عامر
rows.claim: Asim and Abdullah ibn Amir read qawla in the accusative as a circumstantial expression meaning I speak truthfully; the gesture in dhalika governs it.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وعبد الله بن عامر «قول الحق» بالنصب على الحال

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj treats the accusative as a verbal noun, meaning I speak the true statement, implied by what precedes.
rows.anchor: هو مصدر أي أقول قول الحق لأن ما قبله يدل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other readings of the phrase are praise or exhortation; Abdullah reads qala al-haqq, and Hasan reads qawl with damma, as in the related wording in al-Anam.
rows.anchor: وقيل: مدح. وقيل: إغراء. وقرأ عبد الله «قال الحق». وقرأ الحسن «قول الحق» بضم القاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alladhi modifies Jesus; yamtarun means either they doubt or differ about him.
rows.anchor: الذي } من نعت عيسى. { فيه يمترون } أي يشكون أي ذلك عيسى ابن مريم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada’s report says Israelite factions selected four learned representatives to dispute Jesus after he was raised: Jacobites called him God, Nestorians God’s son, another faction one of three deities including his mother, and the fourth said he was God’s servant and messenger; each acquired followers and fought, with the Muslims prevailing.
rows.anchor: قال: اجتمع بنو إسرائيل فأخرجوا منهم أربعة نفر، أخرج كل قوم عالمهم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the parties in the verse were those who differed over Jesus and became factions.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: وهم الذين قال الله تعالى فيهم: { فاختلف الأحزاب من بينهم } اختلفوا فيه فصاروا أحزابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Mary, Jesus, and her cousin fled to Egypt, where they remained twelve years until the king they feared died.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: فمر بمريم ابن عمها ومعها ابنها إلى مصر فكانوا فيها اثنتي عشرة سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi relates an account he found in Egyptian history and an apparent Gospel: Herod ruled at Jesus’s Bethlehem birth, God told Joseph in a dream to take the child and mother to Egypt, and Joseph obeyed.
rows.anchor: وجاء في الإنجيل الظاهر أن السيد المسيح لما ولد في بيت لحم كان هيرودس في ذلك الوقت ملكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Egyptian account locates their arrival at the balsam well outside Cairo, where Mary washed Jesus’s clothes; the plant and baptismal oil were rare and esteemed gifts among Christian rulers.
rows.anchor: نزل ببئر البلسان التي بظاهر القاهرة، وغسلت ثيابه على ذلك البئر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They reached Ashmunin and Qusqam, now called al-Muharraqa, which Christians still honor and visit at Easter as the farthest point Jesus reached in Egypt before returning to Syria.
rows.anchor: وصل السيد المسيح إلى مدينة الأشمونين وقسقام المعروفة الآن بالمحرقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is neither fitting nor possible for God to take a son; min is an augmentative particle and an is the subject of kana, expressing that son-taking is not God’s attribute.
rows.anchor: ما كان لله } أي ما ينبغي له ولا يجوز { أن يتخذ من ولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is exalted above having a child; when He decrees a matter, He only says Be and it is, a point Qurtubi discussed under al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: ثم نزه نفسه تعالى عن مقالتهم فقال: { سبحانه } أن يكون له ولد

rows.speaker: أهل المدينة وابن كثير وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: The Medinans, Ibn Kathir, and Abu Amr read anna with an open hamza.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل المدينة وابن كثير وأبو عمرو بفتح «أن

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة
rows.claim: The Kufans read inna with a kasra, as a new sentence; Ubayy’s reading without the conjunction also supports this parsing.
rows.anchor: وأهل الكوفة «وإن» بكسر الهمزة على أنه مستأنف

rows.speaker: الخليل وسيبويه
rows.claim: Al-Khalil and Sibawayh parse the open form as a causal clause, with anna in the accusative after an omitted li; they compare the construction concerning mosques belonging to God.
rows.anchor: فمذهب الخليل وسيبويه أن المعنى ولأن الله ربي وربكم

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra allows the open form to be genitive after an omitted li, either causally or as an extension of the command to pray and give zakat while alive.
rows.anchor: وأجاز الفراء أن يكون في موضع خفض على حذف اللام

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisa’i allows the open form to be nominative, meaning the matter is that God is my Lord and yours.
rows.anchor: وأجاز الكسائي أن يكون في موضع رفع بمعنى والأمر أن الله ربي وربكم

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
rows.claim: Abu Amr ibn al-Ala reportedly parses the phrase as an object of decreeing: God decreed that He is Lord; on this analysis one cannot begin a sentence at anna.
rows.anchor: أبو عبيد أن أبا عمرو بن العلاء قاله، وهو أن يكون المعنى: وقضى أن الله ربي وربكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship God because He is the true, straight religion without deviation.
rows.anchor: فاعبدوه هذا صراط مستقيم } أي دين قويم لا اعوجاج فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min is redundant in the phrase about parties differing; Qatada understands it as meaning among themselves.
rows.anchor: من» زائدة أي اختلف الأحزاب بينهم. وقال قتادة: أي ما بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The factions of the People of the Book disputed Jesus: Jews accused him of magic, while Nestorians called him God’s son, Melkites one of three, and Jacobites God; Christians exaggerated and Jews fell short.
rows.anchor: فاليهود بالقدح والسحر. والنصارى قالت النسطورية منهم: هو ابن الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the parties were the polytheists who organized against Muhammad and rejected him.
rows.anchor: المراد بالأحزاب الذين تحزبوا على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وكذبوه من المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mishhad can mean witnessing Judgment Day as an event, the attendance occurring then, or the place where all creatures assemble.
rows.anchor: أي من شهود يوم القيامة، والمشهد بمعنى المصدر، والشهود الحضور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the scene as the gathering where they conferred and resolved to disbelieve in God and call Him one of three.
rows.anchor: فأجمعوا على الكفر بالله، وقولهم: إن الله ثالث ثلاثة

rows.speaker: أبو العباس
rows.claim: Abu al-Abbas says asma‘ bihim and absir bihim are Arabic exclamations, expressing amazement at their acute hearing and sight on the Day of Judgment.
rows.anchor: العرب تقول هذا في موضع التعجب فتقول: أسمع بزيد وأبصر بزيد

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says no one will hear or see better than they do when God questions Jesus, as in the passage about taking him and his mother as deities.
rows.anchor: لا أحد أسمع منهم يوم القيامة ولا أبصر، حين يقول الله تبارك وتعالى لعيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes asma‘ mean obedience: they will be most obedient to God on that day.
rows.anchor: وقيل: «أسمع» بمعنى الطاعة أي ما أطوعهم لله في ذلك اليوم

rows.speaker: قتادة وغيره
rows.claim: The wrongdoers are plainly astray today by calling a human being—born, eating, drinking, relieving himself, and needing things—a god; they will hear and see when punishment arrives, but it will not help them.
rows.anchor: وأي ضلال أبين من أن يعتقد المرء في شخص مثله حملته الأرحام، وأكل وشرب، وأحدث واحتاج أنه إله

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud says everyone who enters Hell has a house in Paradise that they regret losing.
rows.anchor: ما من أحد يدخل النار إلا وله بيت في الجنة فيتحسر عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view locates the regret when a person receives the record in the left hand.
rows.anchor: وقيل: تقع الحسرة إذا أعطي كتابه بشماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The affair is concluded when judgment ends, the people of Paradise enter Paradise, and the people of Hell enter Hell.
rows.anchor: أهل الجنة الجنة وأهل النار النار

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: In Sahih Muslim, Abu Sa‘id transmits the Prophet’s report that death appears as a speckled ram between Paradise and Hell, is recognized by both groups and slaughtered, after which each is told it will live forever; the Prophet cites this verse.
rows.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi says the same report is related in similar form by Bukhari from Ibn Umar, Ibn Majah from Abu Hurayra, and al-Tirmidhi from Abu Sa‘id, who grades it hasan sahih.
rows.anchor: خرجه البخاري بمعناه عن ابن عمر، وابن ماجه من حديث أبي هريرة، والترمذي عن أبي سعيد يرفعه وقال فيه حديث حسن صحيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi says these reports and verses prove the unbelievers remain in Hell forever, refuting claims that divine wrath ends or that Iblis, Pharaoh, Haman, and Qarun enter Paradise.
rows.anchor: وبينا هناك أن الكفار مخلدون بهذه الأحاديث والآي ردا على من قال: إن صفة الغضب تنقطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God inherits the earth by putting its inhabitants to death; they return to Him for recompense according to their deeds.
rows.anchor: أي نميت سكانها فنرثها. { وإلينا يرجعون } يوم القيامة فنجازي كلا بعمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad is told to recite Abraham’s story from the Qur’an; Abraham was their ancestor, a sincere monotheist who did not worship idols, so the audience should not do so either.
rows.anchor: اقرأ عليهم يا محمد في القرآن أمر إبراهيم فقد عرفوا أنهم من ولده، فإنه كان حنيفا مسلما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s father was Azar, as discussed earlier; Abraham asks why he worships idols that cannot hear, see, or benefit him.
rows.anchor: لم تعبد } أي لأي شيء تعبد: { ما لا يسمع ولا يبصر ولا يغني عنك شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham says he has received certainty about God and the afterlife, including punishment for worshiping other than God, and invites his father to follow him to a saving, straight religion.
rows.anchor: أي من اليقين والمعرفة بالله وما يكون بعد الموت، وأن من عبد غير الله عذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not worshiping Satan means not obeying him in disbelief, since obedience to anyone in sin is worship; Satan has rebelled against the Merciful.
rows.anchor: أي لا تطعه فيما يأمرك به من الكفر، ومن أطاع شيئا في معصية فقد عبده

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisa’i says asiyyan and asin mean the same thing.
rows.anchor: وعصيا وعاص بمعنى واحد قاله الكسائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kana may be an extra particle, mean became, or describe a continuing state.
rows.anchor: صلة زائدة. وقيل: كان بمعنى صار. وقيل: بمعنى الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A threat from the Merciful would touch Abraham’s father if he died persisting in his present state; akhafu may mean I know, or express fear that he die an unbeliever.
rows.anchor: أي إن مت على ما أنت عليه. ويكون «أخاف» بمعنى أعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being Satan’s ally means becoming his companion in the Fire.
rows.anchor: فتكون للشيطان وليا } أي قرينا في النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s father asks whether he is turning away from his gods.
rows.anchor: أي أترغب عنها إلى غيرها

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says Abraham’s father threatened to stone him.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: يعني بالحجارة. الضحاك: بالقول أي لأشتمنك

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says the threat means he would verbally abuse Abraham.
rows.anchor: الضحاك: بالقول أي لأشتمنك. ابن عباس: لأضربنك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the threat means he would beat Abraham.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس: لأضربنك. وقيل: لأظهرن أمرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation of the threat is that he would expose or publicize Abraham’s affair.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لأظهرن أمرك. { واهجرني مليا }

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets leave me for a long while as withdrawing safely, without harm from his father; al-Tabari prefers this, and Qurtubi notes that it makes the word circumstantial for Abraham.
rows.anchor: أي اعتزلني سالم العرض لا يصيبنك مني معرة واختاره الطبري

rows.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد
rows.claim: Hasan and Mujahid interpret the phrase as leave me for a long period, deriving it from a word for a stretch of time.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن ومجاهد: «مليا» دهرا طويلا

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisa’i records several forms meaning a long span of time; on that interpretation the word functions adverbially.
rows.anchor: قال الكسائي: يقال هجرته مليا وملوة وملوة وملاوة وملاوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham did not answer his father harshly because he had not been commanded to fight him for disbelief.
rows.anchor: لم يعارضه إبراهيم عليه السلام بسوء الرد لأنه لم يؤمر بقتاله على كفره

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most interpreters take Abraham’s greeting as peaceful disengagement rather than a salutation; al-Tabari glosses it as safety from him, which supports not initiating greetings with unbelievers.
rows.anchor: والجمهور على أن المراد بسلامه المسالمة التي هي المتاركة لا التحية

rows.speaker: النقاش
rows.claim: Al-Naqqash says Abraham, being forbearing, answered a fool gently, as in the verse about servants of the Merciful.
rows.anchor:
حليم خاطب سفيها كما قال:
وإذا خاطبهم الجاهلون قالوا سلاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take Abraham’s words as a farewell greeting, allowing a greeting to an unbeliever and permitting one to initiate it.
rows.anchor: هو تحية مفارق وجوز تحية الكافر وأن يبدأ بها

rows.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
rows.claim: Sufyan ibn Uyayna permits greeting a non-hostile unbeliever, citing God’s permission to treat them kindly and Abraham’s example.
rows.anchor: قيل لابن عيينة: هل يجوز السلام على الكافر؟ قال: نعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi says the strongest reading of the verse is Sufyan ibn Uyayna’s permission to greet unbelievers.
rows.anchor: قلت: الأظهر من الآية ما قاله سفيان بن عيينة

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A sound report from Abu Hurayra says the Prophet forbade initiating greetings to Jews and Christians and instructed Muslims to make them take the narrower side of the road.
rows.anchor:
روى أبو هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:
" لا تبدؤوا اليهود والنصارى بالسلام

rows.speaker: أسامة بن زيد
rows.claim: A report in both Sahihs from Usama ibn Zayd describes the Prophet greeting a mixed gathering of Muslims, polytheists, and Jews while visiting Sa‘d ibn Ubada before Badr.
rows.anchor:
وفي الصحيحين عن أسامة بن زيد:
" أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ركب حمارا
